title: You'd Give It All For This
author: The Daily Dad
summary: The Daily Dad draws on a podcast moment in which comedian Bert Kreischer walks into a friend's bathroom and sees two small stools with children's names on them -- the kind toddlers use to reach the sink. He hadn't seen those in his own home in 12 years and became emotional: 'I would give it all.' He would give it all to be back in a house with children that young. The piece uses this moment to reflect on a universal parental experience: the exhausting, loud, sticky, chaotic years of early childhood that parents count down through and then desperately wish back. The message is simple but urgent -- you are living right now in moments your future self will ache for, that other parents are jealous of. You cannot slow time or freeze the season. But you can be present: put the phone down, stay a little longer at bedtime, say yes to one more story. Because one day you will walk into a quiet house, see something small that used to matter, and think the same thing Bert did.
points: * Bert Kreischer's reaction to two small bathroom stools with children's names on them captures the universal parental experience: the years that felt exhausting become the years you'd give everything to return to. * The exhausting years -- loud, sticky, chaotic, where you count down to bedtime -- are the very years your future self will ache for most. * You are living right now in moments that other parents are jealous of; you cannot slow time or freeze the season but you can be present. * The small, specific, forgettable details of early childhood -- the step stools, the trailing ducks, the sleeping kid carried in arms -- are what become unbearably meaningful in retrospect. * Practical presence: put the phone down, stay a little longer at bedtime, say yes to one more story -- because these are the deposits your future self will want to draw on.
